text:
erin: flagging a pattern: postmortem actions often sit without SLA. propose we add a simple escalation SLA for owners.
tomo: agree. what do you mean by SLA here?
erin: owner must confirm ETA within 48h, implement or update status weekly, and reach final verification by 30d. if owner misses 48h confirm -> escalate to IC.
isabel: add a second escalation at 14d if progress stalls. IC can reassign or schedule a mini-sprint.
sam: suggest we formalize this in the runbook and have incident-bot enforce reminders and escalate in channel.
devops-bot: Reminder template created: "pm-action-confirm" 48h, "pm-action-check" 14d, "pm-action-verify" 30d.
erin: also want a rota tweak: IC rotation to 5 weeks (instead of 6) for better overlap with product cycles. pilot 3 months.
tomo: ok to pilot, but require a short IC handoff note template for continuity.
isabel: propose metrics we track during pilot: percent actions with ETA at 48h, percent closed by 30d, number of escalations, owner-transfer count.
sam: i'll add SLA language + escalation flow to runbook. devops-bot, can you add auto-assign escalation pings when 48h or 14d missed?
devops-bot: Escalation automation scheduled: @IC on call is pinged when SLA triggered.
erin: immediate tasks: 1) runbook update (sam) due Wed; 2) add automation (tomo + devops-bot) due Fri; 3) create quick dashboard for SLA metrics (isabel) due next Tue.
isabel: noted, will draft a tiny dashboard showing the three metrics.
tomo: i'll coordinate devops-bot triggers and test on a sample postmortem.
erin: thanks all. let's run this pilot for 3 months and review at retro. low friction is key.
